items.title: Sensory-based non-pharmacological interventions for reducing dental anxiety and improving behavioural cooperation in paediatric patients: a systematic review with GRADE assessment.

ai.headline: Sensory changes like adapted dental rooms, screens or music may lower children's dental anxiety and improve cooperation, but evidence is only moderate at best.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 47 studies, including 25 randomised or controlled trials, looked at sensory-based approaches such as sensory-adapted dental environments, audiovisual distraction or virtual reality, music therapy, aromatherapy and weighted blankets for children up to 18 years old. The strongest evidence supported sensory-adapted dental environments and audiovisual distraction or virtual reality, while music therapy had lower certainty; overall certainty ranged from very low to moderate because of bias, varied methods and imprecise results.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that simple, non-drug changes to the dental setting may help anxious children, though more high-quality research is needed before they become routine.
ai.life_skill: If a child feels anxious about dental visits, ask the dental team whether a calmer environment, headphones, music or a video could be used during treatment.
ai.fact: Dental anxiety affects an estimated 9%-20% of children and disproportionately impacts those with neurodevelopmental conditions.

quiz.answer: Sensory-adapted dental environments and audiovisual distraction or virtual reality had moderate-certainty evidence, the strongest among the approaches reviewed.

ai.caveat: This is a systematic review of trials with overall low-to-moderate certainty, limited by risk of bias, heterogeneity and imprecise results, so it supports cautious use rather than proof of routine benefit.

items.title: Neonatal Sleep Disruption and Brain Development in Preterm Infants: A Narrative Review of Neurodevelopmental Outcomes

ai.headline: Sleep disruption in preterm babies may be linked to later brain and behaviour outcomes, but proof is limited.
ai.summary: The review looked at studies of preterm infants in neonatal intensive care and how noise, light, caregiving and painful procedures can disrupt sleep. It found that sleep disruption is linked to altered brain development, attention problems, attachment difficulties and stress system changes, though causes are hard to separate from prematurity and illness.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that protecting sleep in neonatal units could be a practical way to support long-term development in preterm babies.
ai.life_skill: Notice how noise, light and frequent handling might affect a baby’s sleep and consider quieter, clustered care where possible.
ai.fact: Sleep supports brain maturation, synaptic plasticity and white matter development in newborns.

quiz.question: What does the review say about the link between neonatal sleep disruption and later outcomes?
quiz.answer: It is linked to altered brain development, attention problems, attachment difficulties and stress system changes, but causal relationships remain difficult to establish.

ai.caveat: This is a narrative review of observational studies and meta-analyses, not a randomised trial, so it cannot prove that sleep disruption causes later problems.

ai.headline: AI feedback improved writing as much as teacher feedback, but students felt less motivated by it.
ai.summary: A randomized trial compared AI-generated feedback, teacher feedback, and no feedback for undergraduate students revising essays. items.title: Green HRM, Green Leadership and Work Engagement in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Bibliometric–Systematic Review and Research Framework for Environmental Sustainability

items.title: Neuropsychiatric symptom clusters and plasma proteomic signatures across cognitive ageing and dementia in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo: a cross-sectional analysis of the EVCD-RDC cohort

ai.headline: In older adults in Kinshasa, certain blood proteins were linked to neuropsychiatric symptoms and depression scores.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 779 older adults with available blood protein data from a cohort of 1044 in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. items.title: Nicotinic receptor in dopamine neurons mediates learned odor choice

ai.headline: A nicotinic receptor in fruit-fly reward neurons helps flies choose a learned odor when two odors compete.
ai.summary: Researchers studied fruit flies to see how a nicotinic acetylcholine receptor called Dα1 in dopamine neurons affects odor-sugar learning. Flies lacking Dα1 in these neurons had weaker odor-evoked signals and struggled to pick the rewarded odor when choosing between two odors, while their response to sugar and innate odor choices stayed intact.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how acetylcholine and dopamine interact in reward circuits to support value-based decisions when faced with competing options.

ai.fact: In fruit flies, dopamine neurons in the PAM cluster convey sugar reward signals and promote approach toward a rewarded odor after associative learning.

quiz.question: What happened when Dα1 was knocked down in fruit-fly reward neurons?
quiz.answer: Odor-evoked synaptic signals were weakened and learned odor choice between two competing odors was impaired, while sugar responses and innate odor choice were largely preserved.

ai.caveat: The study was done in fruit flies, so the findings may not directly apply to humans.

items.title: Less than 42 minutes of bright daylight linked to higher dementia risk

ai.summary: Researchers studied daylight exposure in 87,000 adults and found higher exposure was associated with lower dementia risk. They discovered that less than 42 minutes of bright daylight daily was a strong predictor of dementia. The study suggests a link between daylight and brain health.

ai.life_skill: Spend time outside during the day to get natural daylight

items.title: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps

ai.headline: AI agents can learn to navigate live iPhone apps through online reinforcement learning with step-by-step feedback.
ai.summary: Researchers trained AI agents to navigate live iOS apps using an online reinforcement learning framework that splits tasks into planning and screen-grounding components. items.title: Assessment and Treatment for Chronic Pain in Veterans With Serious Mental Illness

ai.summary: The study looks at Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Chronic Pain in veterans who also have serious mental illness. It checks whether the therapy is practical and acceptable, and examines how pain and mental health symptoms affect each other.

items.title: EPF/EPFL Peptide Signaling as a Regulatory Node Linking Stomatal Development to Drought and Heat Tolerance in Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.)

ai.headline: Tomato genes that shape leaf pores respond differently to drought and heat depending on the plant variety.
ai.summary: Researchers identified 15 EPF/EPFL genes in tomato that are linked to stomatal development and guard cell differentiation. quiz.question: What did the study find about EPF/EPFL gene activity in the two tomato varieties under stress?
quiz.answer: The genes showed distinct, genotype- and stress-dependent expression patterns under drought, heat, and combined drought-heat stress.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and it reports gene-expression patterns rather than proof that these genes cause drought or heat tolerance.

items.title: Waves alter Antarctic polynyas by breaking up surrounding sea ice

ai.headline: Ocean waves help keep Antarctic polynyas open by breaking up nearby sea ice.
ai.summary: The study looked at polynyas, areas of open water surrounded by Antarctic sea ice. It found that waves breaking up surrounding sea ice play a role in maintaining these open-water areas alongside winds.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain how Antarctic open-water areas form and stay open, which affects ocean-atmosphere exchange and marine life.

quiz.question: What helps maintain Antarctic polynyas according to the study?

items.title: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers

ai.headline: Blocking a cancer-related enzyme slowed tumour growth and extended survival in mice with different cancers.
ai.summary: Researchers tested a drug that inhibits METTL1, an enzyme involved in m7G methylation, in several mouse models of solid and blood cancers. The treatment impaired tumour growth and substantially prolonged survival across models of different tissue origin.

items.title: Revealing the benefit of eye motion for acuity under emulated cone loss

ai.headline: Tiny eye movements help people see clearly even when many cone cells are inactive.
ai.summary: Researchers used a system to mimic cone cell loss in healthy eyes by switching off stimulation to selected cones. They found that visual acuity gets worse as more cones are lost, but natural eye movements partly compensate by letting the remaining cones gather more information from what is being viewed.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain why vision can stay surprisingly good despite retinal disease and shows how ordinary eye movements support sight.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your eyes make tiny movements when you look at something, and let them move naturally rather than staring rigidly.
ai.fact: Clinically normal visual acuity can persist despite up to 50% of cone cells being lost.

ai.why_it_matters: It shows that physical symbols can keep old social rules alive even after laws change, which helps explain why cultural shifts take time.
ai.life_skill: Notice how visible symbols in your community might reinforce certain expectations or norms.
ai.fact: Social norms can persist and influence behaviour even after the formal authority that enforced them is removed.

quiz.question: Where were the increases in female employment and schooling largest?
quiz.answer: The increases were largest in areas where no religious monument survived the ban.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint based on a historical natural experiment, so it shows a link rather than proving that removing symbols directly causes norm changes.

items.title: Spinal cord injury can reshape gut microbes that influence whole-body health

ai.headline: Spinal cord injuries may change gut bacteria, which could affect overall body health and healing.
ai.summary: Researchers examined the genetic makeup of gut microbes in people with spinal cord injuries. They found early signs that these microbial changes are linked to inflammation and immune function, suggesting they might play a role in the healing process.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights that an injury to the spine can have effects far beyond the nervous system, influencing the internal ecosystem that supports general health.
ai.life_skill: Notice that physical health issues can sometimes have unexpected connections to other body systems, like digestion.
ai.fact: Gut microbial communities can be reshaped by spinal cord injuries, potentially influencing whole-body inflammation.

quiz.question: What did the study suggest about the relationship between spinal cord injuries and gut microbes?
quiz.answer: The study suggests that spinal cord injuries can reshape gut microbes, which may influence inflammation and immune function.

ai.caveat: This is a news report describing early study results, not a peer-reviewed publication, so the findings are preliminary and not yet confirmed.

items.title: In Dark Eden, I imagined how life might exist on a sunless planet

ai.headline: A science-fiction author explains how he imagined life on a sunless rogue planet outside the Milky Way.
ai.summary: The piece describes how Chris Beckett thought through the science behind Dark Eden, a novel set on a rogue planet with no sun. It covers his reasoning about how life might exist in permanent darkness.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how scientific ideas can be used to imagine worlds very different from Earth.
ai.life_skill: Notice how authors use real science to build imaginary settings.
ai.fact: Rogue planets are planets that travel through space without orbiting a star.

quiz.question: What kind of planet is Dark Eden set on?
quiz.answer: A rogue planet outside the Milky Way with no sun.

ai.caveat: This is a news article about a novel, not a scientific study, so it reports imagination and commentary rather than tested evidence.

items.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.

ai.headline: Deep learning can help diagnose brain diseases from EEG scans, but is not yet ready for routine clinics.
ai.summary: This systematic review examined studies using deep learning to analyse EEG brain recordings for diagnosing neurological diseases. It found that models such as CNNs, RNNs and transformers can detect conditions including epilepsy, Alzheimer’s disease and Parkinson’s disease, but challenges remain around data, interpretability and clinical use.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI may one day support faster, more objective diagnosis of brain disorders from routine EEG tests.
ai.fact: EEG is a non-invasive way to record brain activity and is widely used to help diagnose neurological diseases.

quiz.question: Which brain diseases does the review say deep-learning EEG models may help diagnose?
quiz.answer: The review lists epilepsy, Alzheimer’s disease, encephalopathy, Parkinson’s disease, mild cognitive impairment, sleep disorders and developmental brain disorders.

ai.caveat: The review summarises existing research rather than providing new clinical proof, and the authors note that translating these models into everyday medical practice remains difficult.

items.title: Impact of COVID-19 on adolescent mental health in Albania

ai.headline: In Albania, girls and older teenagers reported worse mental health impacts from the pandemic than boys or younger peers.
ai.summary: This study surveyed over 5,000 Albanian adolescents aged 11–15 in 2022 about their mental health during the pandemic. It found that roughly 35% reported a negative impact, with girls and older teenagers significantly more likely to report this than boys or younger students.
ai.why_it_matters: It highlights that mental health struggles during crises are not evenly distributed, suggesting that support systems need to specifically address the needs of older adolescents and girls.
ai.life_skill: Notice that stress affects different people differently, and check in with friends to see if they are struggling even if they seem fine.
ai.fact: In this Albanian study, family wealth and whether parents were employed did not predict whether adolescents reported negative mental health impacts from the pandemic.

quiz.question: Which two groups of Albanian adolescents were most likely to report negative mental health impacts from COVID-19?
quiz.answer: Girls and older adolescents were significantly more likely to perceive negative mental health impact.

ai.caveat: This is a single cross-sectional study relying on self-reported data, so it cannot prove causation or account for changes in mental health over time.

items.title: Quality of life among vocational rehabilitation patients with mild work-related disability and its association with return-to-work outcomes

ai.headline: Better quality of life after rehabilitation is linked to a higher chance of returning to work for injured employees.
ai.summary: A study followed 343 employees with mild work-related disability who received vocational rehabilitation. Their health-related quality of life improved in several areas, and those who returned to work—either to their original job or a new one—reported better quality-of-life scores at discharge than those who did not return.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that feeling healthier and more capable after an injury may be linked to getting back into work.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether your confidence about returning to work changes as your health improves, and discuss any concerns with your rehabilitation team.
ai.fact: Better quality of life at discharge is positively associated with return-to-work outcomes after vocational rehabilitation.

quiz.question: What did the study find about quality-of-life scores at discharge for people who returned to work compared with those who did not?
quiz.answer: People who returned to their original post or a new post had significantly higher quality-of-life scores in several areas than those who did not return to work.

ai.caveat: This is a single observational study from one hospital, so it cannot prove that better quality of life causes a return to work.

items.title: Early career challenges of physical education teachers

ai.headline: New PE teachers face location, training and support challenges in their first five years.
ai.summary: This study interviewed 25 physical education teachers in Türkiye within their first five years of teaching. It found they struggled with local climate, transport and culture, felt unprepared for administration, classroom management and assessment due to a theory-practice gap in training, and lacked support from administrators, students and parents.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that new teachers’ success depends on both personal resources and workplace support, not just individual effort.
ai.life_skill: Notice which parts of a new job feel hardest and ask a trusted colleague or mentor for specific help.
ai.fact: Early-career physical education teachers in Türkiye report adaptation difficulties linked to geographic, pedagogical and social factors.

quiz.question: What three main themes did the study find in early-career PE teachers’ challenges?
quiz.answer: Regional and psychosocial dynamics, PETE and perceived professional competence, and stakeholder relationships and perceived social support.

ai.caveat: This is a small qualitative case study in one country, so its findings are not proof and may not apply elsewhere.

items.title: Multistep and Multivariate Time Series Explainability with GradientSHAP: A Wind Power Case Study

ai.headline: A new method helps explain AI wind power forecasts by showing which weather factors matter most.
ai.summary: The study adapted a technique called GradientSHAP to make AI models for predicting wind power easier to understand. It found that, with careful handling and expert knowledge, the method can reveal how environmental and site-specific factors influence forecasts across multiple time steps.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding how AI predicts wind power can help grid operators manage renewable energy more reliably as the world moves away from fossil fuels.
ai.life_skill: Try asking how an AI tool reaches its conclusion before trusting its recommendation.
ai.fact: Wind power is variable and intermittent, which creates challenges for integrating it into electricity grids.

quiz.question: What did the researchers adapt GradientSHAP to do in this study?
quiz.answer: They adapted it to provide interpretability for multivariate, multistep wind power forecasting.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, so its findings are not yet established.

items.title: Eye See Your Intentions: Age-Related Differences in Gaze Perception and Trustworthiness Attributions

ai.headline: Older adults are more likely to see averted gaze as direct and rate those faces as more trustworthy.
ai.summary: Researchers tested 307 adults aged 18 to 88 online using faces with different expressions and gaze directions. As age increased, people were more likely to perceive averted gaze as direct, especially for non-fearful expressions, and greater perceived direct gaze was linked to higher trustworthiness ratings, particularly among older adults.
ai.why_it_matters: This may help explain why older adults sometimes place greater trust in others and could be more vulnerable to deception.
ai.life_skill: Notice where someone’s eyes are actually pointing before deciding whether they seem trustworthy.
ai.fact: Direct gaze is generally interpreted as an approach signal, while averted gaze is interpreted as an avoidance signal.

quiz.question: What happened to trustworthiness ratings as perceived direct gaze increased?
quiz.answer: Greater perception of direct gaze was associated with greater facial trustworthiness attributions.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the online design cannot prove that age causes these differences in gaze perception or trust judgments.

items.title: Synthetic Reception: Manufacturing the Signals of Uptake in Hype and Technology Expectations

ai.headline: Companies can secretly fake signs that lots of people like a new technology to make it seem popular.
ai.summary: The paper studies how hype is created not just by promises but by how audiences receive them. It introduces “synthetic reception,” where producers hide their own role in creating signals of uptake—such as likes, early reactions or endorsements—so they look like independent audience judgements.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps people question whether apparent public excitement about a new app, device or trend is genuine or manufactured.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether excitement about a new technology comes from many independent voices or looks like a coordinated campaign.
ai.fact: Signals of uptake such as counts, first reactions and endorsements shape what audiences decide deserves attention.

quiz.question: What does “synthetic reception” fake?
quiz.answer: It fakes the independence of a signal of uptake, making a producer’s concealed contribution look like independent audience judgement.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed and offers a conceptual framework rather than tested evidence.

items.title: Quantifying Localized Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes by Deep Learning on H&E Images: Analytical Validation and Prognostic Value in Lung Adenocarcinoma

ai.headline: An AI tool that maps immune cells in lung cancer tissue may predict survival better than current tests.
ai.summary: Researchers developed an AI method called the focal TIL score that measures immune cell density in specific areas of lung cancer tissue using standard pathology images. In a study of 685 patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors, higher focal TIL scores were linked to longer overall survival and outperformed the standard PD-L1 biomarker.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI could make cancer prognosis more objective and standardised using images hospitals already produce.

quiz.question: What did the focal TIL score measure in lung cancer tissue?
quiz.answer: It measured the density of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes within specific tiles across the tissue region.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the survival finding comes from an observational association rather than a randomised trial.

items.title: “The significance of context”: Fit, friction, and function in the work lives of early career academics with ADHD

ai.headline: Academia can suit early-career academics with ADHD, but institutional pressures often block that potential.
ai.summary: Researchers interviewed early-career academics with ADHD about their work experiences. They found that ADHD traits can bring strengths such as curiosity and exploration, but social and institutional pressures often make it harder to thrive. The study argues that both individual careers and collective knowledge production can benefit when universities include and support neurodivergent academics.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how workplace context shapes whether neurodivergent traits help or hinder people at work.
ai.life_skill: Notice which work settings help you focus and which create friction, and consider asking for adjustments that suit your needs.
ai.fact: ADHD traits can include both challenges, such as time management, and strengths, such as curiosity-driven exploration.

quiz.question: What did the study suggest about academia for early-career academics with ADHD?
quiz.answer: Academia can be rewarding for them, but social and institutional pressures often inhibit that potential.

ai.caveat: This is a small interview-based study, so its findings cannot be generalised to all academics with ADHD or proven to apply universally.

items.title: 128,000-year-old ice in Tibet could rewrite climate history

ai.headline: Ancient ice found in Tibet
ai.summary: Scientists discovered ancient ice in Tibet that may be over 128,000 years old, preserving a record of Earth's climate. The ice provides a glimpse into the last ice age and could reshape understanding of glacier survival. The discovery reveals new information about Earth's climate history.
ai.why_it_matters: This discovery could change our understanding of how glaciers respond to climate change, impacting everyday life and the environment.
ai.life_skill: Explore how climate change affects your local environment.
ai.fact: Ancient ice in Tibet may be over 128,000 years old.

quiz.question: How old is the ancient ice found in Tibet?
quiz.answer: The ancient ice may be more than 128,000 years old.

ai.caveat: The discovery is reported in a news article and may not have been peer-reviewed, so the findings should be treated with caution.

items.title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker

ai.headline: One AI model can both rerank search results and generate answers, saving memory and time.
ai.summary: The study tested Glance, a system that lets a single 9-billion-parameter AI model score and rerank retrieved passages using a lightweight adapter instead of running a separate reranking model. On two retrieval datasets it matched or beat a strong reranker, and on 300 HotpotQA questions it improved answer quality by a small but statistically supported margin.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how AI search tools could become faster and cheaper to run by using one model for several jobs instead of many.
ai.life_skill: Try checking whether an AI answer cites its sources before trusting it.
ai.fact: Glance achieved nDCG@10 of 0.741 on SciFact and 0.345 on NFCorpus, compared with 0.721 and 0.326 for bge-reranker-v2-m3.

quiz.question: What did Glance use to score candidate passages without prefilling each pair separately?
quiz.answer: A lightweight decision adapter and pointer head branching from a shared cached context.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and evaluation covers only two retrieval datasets, one QA dataset and one backbone family.

items.title: Impact Of Early Cognitive Rehabilitation On Functional Outcomes Following Moderate Traumatic Brain Injury

ai.headline: Cognitive rehab aids brain injury recovery
ai.summary: This study examined the impact of early cognitive rehabilitation on patients with moderate traumatic brain injury. The study aimed to detect the effect of this rehabilitation on functional outcomes. The results of the study are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding the impact of cognitive rehabilitation can inform treatment approaches for traumatic brain injury patients
ai.life_skill: Try seeking professional help for brain injuries
ai.fact: Cognitive rehabilitation is used to aid recovery from traumatic brain injuries

quiz.question: What type of injury did the study focus on?
quiz.answer: Moderate traumatic brain injury

ai.caveat: The study's findings may not be fully peer-reviewed or published yet

items.title: [Articles] Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial
authors: Martha A Q Curley, Martin C J Kneyber, Ira M Cheifetz, Michele Kong, Sidharth Mahapatra, Adam J Schwarz, Suwannee Phumeetham, Katherine Irby, Natalie Napolitano, Onella S Dawkins-Henry, Emily E Birch, Corrine F Elliott, Lindsay R Berry, Kevin J Downes, Aruna Natarajan, Michelle A Detry, Kert Viele, Todd L Graves, Michael Matthay, Lisa A Asaro, David Wypij, PROSpect Study Investigators, Paediatric Acute Lung Injury and Sepsis Investigators Network

ai.headline: Prone positioning and HFOV not recommended
ai.summary: Researchers studied prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome. They found no evidence to support these strategies as first-line treatments. The study was a randomised controlled trial.
ai.why_it_matters: This finding impacts the treatment of children with acute respiratory distress syndrome, influencing medical decisions and patient care.
ai.fact: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation do not improve ventilator-free days in patients with early, moderate-to-severe paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome.

quiz.question: What was found regarding prone positioning and HFOV in early PARDS?
quiz.answer: No evidence was found to support their use as first-line strategies.

ai.caveat: The study's findings may not apply to all patients or situations beyond the study's parameters.

items.title: A new neural code for position: generalizable spatial maps in mouse medial frontal cortex

ai.headline: Mouse frontal cortex cells may encode position using distances to landmarks, helping navigation.
ai.summary: Researchers imaged brain cells in mice exploring a square arena with landmarks. Activity in the medial frontal cortex could predict the animal’s position even in areas where the model was not trained, unlike cells in the hippocampus or orbitofrontal cortex. A model based on squared distance to multiple landmarks explained this pattern.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a way the brain might generalise known locations to plan routes through new spaces.
ai.life_skill: Notice landmarks around you to help work out where you are in an unfamiliar place.
ai.fact: Medial frontal cortex activity in mice was linked to spatial position across different parts of an arena.

quiz.question: Which brain region showed position predictions that generalised to a new area of the arena?
quiz.answer: The medial frontal cortex, but not the dorsal hippocampus or lateroventral orbitofrontal cortex.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed, and was done in mice, so the findings may not apply to humans.

items.title: New travel tool combines three algorithms to tailor destination recommendations

ai.headline: Researchers built a travel tool that uses three algorithms to suggest destinations based on preferences, budgets and routes.
ai.summary: The paper describes a new tourist recommendation system that combines three algorithms to match destinations to travelers’ preferences, budgets and travel routes. It aims to fix a limitation of digital platforms that often prioritise popularity over practical considerations.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how digital tools could help people plan trips that fit their real-life constraints rather than just popular spots.
ai.life_skill: Try comparing travel suggestions against your own budget and route before picking a destination.
ai.fact: Some digital travel platforms tend to prioritise popularity over practical considerations like budget and route.

quiz.question: What does the new travel tool combine to tailor destination recommendations?
quiz.answer: It combines three algorithms to match destinations to preferences, budgets and travel routes.

ai.caveat: This is a news report about a paper, not the peer-reviewed study itself, so no methods or results can be verified from the abstract.

items.title: This Arabian desert was once a lush paradise. Why did ancient humans avoid it?

ai.headline: Desert was once lush
ai.summary: An expedition studied an Arabian desert that was once a lush paradise. The team found that water alone was not enough for human settlement. Proposals to block sunlight were also considered.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding why ancient humans avoided this area can provide insights into human migration and settlement patterns.
ai.life_skill: Explore how environmental factors influence human decisions
ai.fact: The Arabian desert was once a lush paradise

quiz.question: What was the Arabian desert like in the past?
quiz.answer: It was once a lush paradise.
